chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Muslim blocks the infidel and inherits him, but the infidel does not block the Believer and does not inherit him.
ai.seo_question: How does Islamic inheritance law handle the relationship between Muslims and non-Muslims regarding inheritance exclusion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'hijab al-din' (blocking by religion), establishing that a Muslim heir excludes a non-Muslim relative from inheritance, but the reverse is not true. This asymmetry reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that faith is a prerequisite for inheriting from a Muslim, emphasizing the spiritual superiority of the believer in material succession. The ruling underscores the theological distinction between the community of faith and those outside it in matters of wealth transfer.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The Muslim blocks the infidel and inherits him, but the infidel does not block the Believer and does not inherit him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from al-Hassan ibn Salih who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The Muslim bars a kafir (non-Muslim) and inherits from him, but a kafir cannot bar the believer and cannot inherit from him (believing person).”’
